prompt: The company buys a patent from an inventor for 60,000 cash. Record the purchase.

reasoning: Purchased intangibles are recognised at cost.
The cash outflow is investing.

why_it_matters: Bought intangibles appear on the balance sheet; equivalent ones built internally usually don't. That distorts comparisons.

prompt: The 60,000 patent has 15 years of legal protection but is expected to be useful for 10 years. Record one year's amortisation (no residual value).

reasoning: Amortise over the shorter of legal and useful life: 10 years.

why_it_matters: Amortisation of acquired intangibles is often excluded from 'adjusted' earnings; decide whether it reflects a real cost.

prompt: This year the company spent 30,000 on research and 80,000 on development of a product that now meets all IAS 38 capitalisation criteria. All paid in cash. Record the costs under IFRS.

reasoning: Research is always expensed.
Development is capitalised once technical feasibility, intention, ability, probable benefits, resources and reliable measurement are shown.

why_it_matters: IFRS companies capitalising development report higher EBITDA and CFO than US peers who expense it.
common_trap: Capitalising research, or expensing qualifying development under IFRS.

ifrs_gaap.ifrs: IAS 38: research expensed; development capitalised when six criteria are met.
ifrs_gaap.us_gaap: ASC 730: R&D expensed as incurred (exceptions: certain software development costs).

prompt: The annual test shows goodwill allocated to a cash-generating unit is impaired by 25,000. Record the impairment.

reasoning: Goodwill is tested annually and when there are indicators.
Goodwill impairments can never be reversed.

why_it_matters: A goodwill write-down admits the acquisition price was too high: a capital-allocation report card.
common_trap: Thinking it affects cash or can be reversed later.

prompt: A company pays 1,000,000 for 100% of a business whose identifiable net assets have a fair value of 850,000. Goodwill?

reasoning: Goodwill = consideration − fair value of identifiable net assets = 150,000
explanation.shortcut: Price paid above fair value of what you can identify.

why_it_matters: Goodwill is the premium for synergies and assembled workforce; it must earn a return like any other capital.
common_trap: Using book values of the target's net assets instead of fair values.

prompt: A company has built a famous brand over 50 years. Is the brand on its balance sheet?
options: No: internally generated brands (and goodwill) are not recognised
Only if the company chooses to revalue it

reasoning: IAS 38 prohibits recognising internally generated brands, mastheads and customer lists.
The same brand bought in an acquisition would be recognised.

why_it_matters: Brand-led companies look asset-light with very high ROIC; acquirers of brands look asset-heavy.
common_trap: Comparing ROIC of organic brand builders and acquirers without adjustment.

prompt: How are intangibles with indefinite useful lives (e.g. some broadcast licences) treated?
options: Not amortised; tested for impairment annually and whenever there is an indication

reasoning: Indefinite does not mean infinite; it means no foreseeable limit.
The life assessment is reviewed each year.

why_it_matters: Large indefinite-life intangibles carry impairment risk; check the headroom disclosures.
common_trap: Thinking indefinite-life assets are never written down.

book_ref.section: Impairment of Indefinite-Life Intangibles Other Than Goodwill

prompt: IAS 38 criteria for capitalising development costs

answer.meaning: Capitalise development only when all are shown: technical feasibility; intention to complete; ability to use or sell; probable future economic benefits; adequate resources to complete; reliable measurement of costs.
answer.formula: Mnemonic: PIRATE — Probable benefits, Intention, Resources, Ability, Technical feasibility, Expenditure measurable
answer.interpretation: Costs before all criteria are met stay expensed; no reinstatement later.
answer.high_signals: High capitalisation rate vs peers: aggressive.

why_it_matters: The capitalisation rate (capitalised / total R&D) is a key earnings-quality ratio for tech and auto companies.
common_trap: Capitalising past costs once the criteria are met.

prompt: A cash-generating unit's carrying amount is 1,200 including goodwill of 150. Its recoverable amount is 1,000. By how much is goodwill reduced?

reasoning: Allocated first to goodwill (wiping all 150)
The remaining 50 is allocated pro rata to the CGU's other assets

why_it_matters: Once goodwill is gone, further losses hit operating assets, which can be reversed later; goodwill cannot.
common_trap: Spreading the loss pro rata across all assets including goodwill.

prompt: A buyer pays less than the fair value of the identifiable net assets acquired (a bargain purchase). What does IFRS 3 require?
options: Reassess the identification and measurement, then recognise any remaining excess as a gain in profit or loss
Record negative goodwill as a liability

reasoning: Bargain purchases are rare, so values are re-checked first.
Any remaining difference is an immediate gain.

why_it_matters: Bargain-purchase gains are non-recurring and often follow distressed deals.
common_trap: Treating the gain as operating profit.

answer.meaning: A non-monetary asset without physical substance that is identifiable: either separable (can be sold or licensed) or arising from contractual or legal rights.
answer.formula: Examples: patents, trademarks, licences, customer contracts, software, franchises
answer.interpretation: Goodwill is not identifiable; it is the residual.
answer.high_signals: Large acquired customer relationships: watch amortisation and impairment.

why_it_matters: In acquisitions, more value assigned to amortising intangibles means lower future EPS than if left in goodwill.

prompt: Which activity is research rather than development?
options: Searching for alternative materials with no specific product in mind
Building and testing a pre-production prototype
Designing tools and moulds for a new product
Running a pilot plant for a product about to launch

reasoning: Research is original investigation to gain new knowledge.
Development applies knowledge to a plan or design before commercial production.

why_it_matters: The research/development boundary is where capitalisation judgement sits.
common_trap: Classifying early exploratory work as development to capitalise it.

prompt: How are start-up costs, training costs and advertising campaigns treated under IAS 38?

reasoning: They do not create an identifiable asset the company controls.
They are expensed when incurred.

why_it_matters: Companies sometimes label these 'investments' in presentations; the accounts must expense them.
common_trap: Capitalising advertising because it builds the brand.

prompt: When can an intangible asset be carried under the revaluation model under IAS 38?
options: Only when fair value can be measured by reference to an active market (rare, e.g. some taxi licences or quotas)

reasoning: Most intangibles are unique, so no active market exists.
Hence nearly all intangibles are at cost.

why_it_matters: Book value almost never reflects intangible value; use market-based measures instead.
common_trap: Assuming IFRS lets brands be revalued.

ifrs_gaap.ifrs: IAS 38: revaluation only with an active market.
ifrs_gaap.us_gaap: Revaluation of intangibles is not allowed.

prompt: In an acquisition, the target has a valuable customer list it never recognised. What does the acquirer do?
options: Recognise the customer list separately at fair value (it is identifiable), reducing goodwill
Ignore it because the target didn't recognise it

reasoning: Acquired identifiable intangibles are recognised even if the target never did.
This is why acquirers show intangibles that organic peers don't.

why_it_matters: The purchase price allocation determines future amortisation and EPS.

prompt: How is goodwill treated after acquisition under IFRS compared with US GAAP for public companies?
options: Both: not amortised, tested for impairment at least annually; IFRS tests at CGU level, US GAAP at reporting-unit level
IFRS amortises over 10 years; US GAAP does not

reasoning: Both frameworks use impairment-only approaches for listed companies.
Private US companies may elect to amortise goodwill (PCC alternative).

why_it_matters: Without amortisation, goodwill stays until impaired, so impairments come in large lumps.
common_trap: Assuming goodwill is amortised under IFRS.

prompt: Compare two software companies: A (IFRS) capitalises 40% of its development spend; B (US GAAP) expenses all R&D. How would you put them on a comparable basis?

answer.model_answer: A's EBITDA, EBIT (partly) and CFO are higher because capitalised development moves to investing and is amortised over time; its assets and invested capital are larger. To compare: (1) Expense A's capitalised development in the year (add it back to opex, remove amortisation) to get an 'all-expensed' EBITDA and EBIT. (2) Or capitalise B's R&D with an assumed life to build a comparable asset base. (3) Compare FCF (CFO − capex − capitalised development), which is unaffected by the choice. (4) Look at total R&D as % of revenue, not just the expensed part. Then compare margins and ROIC on the same basis.

reasoning: Name the distortion, then two consistent adjustments.

why_it_matters: Tech valuations on EV/EBITDA are meaningless across GAAPs without this adjustment.

book_ref.section: Evolving Issue: Recognition of R&D and Internally Generated Intangibles

options: As a separate non-current asset line

reasoning: Goodwill is non-current and shown separately (or in intangibles with disclosure).

why_it_matters: Analysts often deduct goodwill to compute tangible book value for credit and bank analysis.
common_trap: Counting goodwill as collateral value in credit analysis.
